standard_prerequisites: Natural-deduction derivation coding: the derivation with Goedel number d is a tuple whose first entry (d)_0 is the number of immediate subderivations, whose remaining entries are the immediate subderivations, and whose last component records the last rule and its discharge label; the function DischargeLabel extracting that label is primitive recursive.
The assumption codification: an assumption derivation is the triple (0, z, n) where z is the Goedel number of the assumed formula and n its discharge label.

SubtreeSeq: the primitive recursive function enumerating the Goedel numbers of all subderivations of a derivation (proved in the computability-recursive-functions unit of the same source tree, proposition subtreeseq; of length bounded by the code).
Bounded quantification, sequence indexing, and concatenation are primitive recursive.
core_obligations: Set up the discharge vocabulary: an occurrence of an assumption is discharged if it appears with label n in a subderivation ending in a rule with discharge label n; A is an undischarged assumption of the derivation if at least one of its occurrences is not discharged, and the author warns that a derivation may contain both discharged and undischarged occurrences of the same formula.

Characterize undischargedness by a path: consider a sequence of derivations starting at the whole derivation, ending at the assumption (A discharged with label n), each step moving to an immediate subderivation, and with no derivation along the path ending in an inference with discharge label n; A is undischarged exactly when such a path exists.

Express the path test primitive recursively: Subseq (s is a subsequence of the SubtreeSeq enumeration) and Subderiv (d is an immediate subderivation of d') are defined by bounded quantification over sequence entries.

Assemble the definition: OpenAssum(z, d) holds iff there is a sequence s below SubtreeSeq(d) which is a subsequence of it, starts with d itself, whose last element is the assumption triple (0, z, n) for some label n, and each consecutive pair of which moves to an immediate subderivation without a discharge-label-n inference; the displayed bounded definition makes this primitive recursive.
proof_roadmap: Concept reduction plus assembly: the substantive step is the path characterization (undischargedness = existence of a label-avoiding derivation path down to the assumption), after which the definition is a bounded packing of Subseq, Subderiv, and DischargeLabel checks over the SubtreeSeq enumeration.
difficulty_reason: The path characterization is a genuine conceptual step (reducing a global discharge property to an existential bounded path through the subderivation tree), and the final definition nests bounded quantifiers over sequences of sequence codes; no induction is needed.
